name: Ships now (approved 11-13)
what: Today's law, unchanged since his 11-13 approval: one dark blue sheet that thickens with depth.
mechanism: Drawn today: RM_ExcavationWalls.SeeThrough lays one sheet (RM_FaceMaterial.SheetMat, the body colour at alpha 1 - Seen) over the opaque floor and walls; things get RM_SubmergeDraw's cover (one colour at one alpha). Nothing moves.

name: Same blue, firm from the first step
what: Today's colour and deep end, but any water at all hides at least 35% of what lies under it.
mechanism: Built (6c668b36a8): the same sheet and cover with ShallowOpacity 0.35 in RM_UnderLiquid.Seen. Nothing moves.

name: Aqua shallows, navy deeps
what: The colour changes with depth: clear aqua at the edge, navy by 4 m, and stronger than today at every depth.
mechanism: The same sheet with a body colour that changes with depth (one more input to SheetTint). Nothing moves.

name: Aqua shallows, navy deeps, at FIRM's strength
what: AQUA's colours with FIRM's strength, so colour and strength can be judged apart.

name: Clear water that loses red
what: Like real clear water: what lies under keeps its texture but loses its red, then its green, with depth, and a faint pale sheen marks the surface. Over the dark pit floor it is darkest (a dark teal) near 2 m; deeper, only the water's own blue shows, clearly bluer and brighter. Things standing in it (colonist, body, table) get the nearest cover the game can draw on them: one colour at one strength.
mechanism: The floor and walls: a per-colour multiply would need a tint quad per band (TintMat, VertexColor shader). Things: only the one-colour cover (as drawn), never the per-colour loss.

name: FIRM, with wet ground and a waterline
what: FIRM's water, but the ground it covers is wet: the pit floor and walls under the water are darker and a little more saturated than the dry pit, a dark wet band runs along the bank just above the water, and a thin pale line marks where the water meets the wall.
mechanism: Wet ground: the floor and drowned-wall quads in SeeThrough get a TintMat quad of the ground's own darker, more saturated colour (VertexColor shader, already used for the floor shade). Wet band: one more TintMat strip, soft-edged by vertex alpha, above the waterline (on the bank at the rim). Waterline: a ShadeMat strip WATERLINE_PX wide at the line, like the walls' light. All static, one redraw per level change. Cannot: wet pawns, items or the ladder (vanilla draws them; only the cover reaches them).

name: FIRM, with a moving, distorted bottom
what: FIRM's water, but what lies on the bottom is visibly rippled: the floor and walls under the water are displaced by moving waves (more with depth), and pale ripple-light lines cross the floor in the shallows. Animated: three frames.
mechanism: Moving bottom: the floor and drowned-wall quads drawn with vanilla's Map/TerrainLavaShallow distortion shader (its _DistortionAmplitude/_DistortionFrequency/_DistortionSpeed, already set by RM_LiquidLooks for tar), one material per depth band so the amplitude grows with depth [guess ~60% that the shader draws a plain ground texture without its own glow: needs a live look]. Ripple light: RM_LiquidSurface's overlay (MoteGlow, additive, drifting by material offset) with a ripple-line texture, on pit water cells, alpha by depth. Cannot: displace pawns, items, the body, the table or the ladder (vanilla draws them; no grab-pass shader in the mod), so they stay sharp on a wavy floor, as in these pictures.

name: FIRM, wet ground plus a gentle moving bottom
what: The research's combination: WET's wet ground, wet band and waterline, with a gentler version of RIPPLE's moving bottom and ripple-light. Animated: three frames.
mechanism: WET's static quads plus RIPPLE's distortion shader and overlay at lower amplitude and strength. Same limits: nothing standing in the water is displaced or wetted; only the floor, the walls and the bank.
